article_lead.description: the expected exponential transform of a random variable that recovers moments and simplifies independent sums when it exists near zero

new_bank_questions.title: A Bernoulli sum through its MGF
new_bank_questions.body: Let X and Y be independent Bernoulli variables with success probability 0.4. Find the MGF of S=X+Y, its mean and variance, and P(S=2). What part fails if X=Y instead?
new_bank_questions.answer: One MGF is 0.6+0.4e^t, so independence gives M_S(t)=(0.6+0.4e^t)². The mean is 0.8, variance 2(0.4)(0.6)=0.48, and P(S=2)=0.4²=0.16. If X=Y, the sum's MGF is 0.6+0.4e^{2t}; the product rule and binomial law do not apply.

new_bank_questions.title: An exponential transform's domain
new_bank_questions.body: For X exponential with rate 3, derive M_X(t), give its domain, then calculate E(X), Var(X) and M_X(2). Why is substituting t=4 into the rational expression invalid as an MGF calculation?
new_bank_questions.answer: Integrating 3e^{-(3-t)x} over x≥0 gives M_X(t)=3/(3-t) for t<3. Thus E(X)=1/3, Var(X)=1/9, and M_X(2)=3. At t=4 the defining integral diverges; the algebraic value -3 is not an expectation.
